The mystai staying in Karawa and the later unnamed sages/dreamwalkers are likely one local collective, but the final dialogue does not explicitly repeat mystai; both dependent interactions and the entity are medium.
The Draconic-inscribed staff has no confident vault match; Staff of the Forest Soul is a separately constructed staff and was not linked.
The book about maws, the two maps, the die, Wellby’s spyglass, the healed herder, the vulture, and the gnoll leader have no asserted vault match.
Canonical identity notes were read only for matching; unrelated later events, dates, comments, and secrets were not used as extraction evidence.
inclusionChoices: Shani and Tharandros each receive one whole conversation despite interjections, language switching, topic changes, and skill checks.
The individual healed herder and speaking vulture have distinctive interactions; no separate card is made for the other wounded herder or ordinary travelers.
Only the gnoll leader is individualized: poison, shouted coordination, and a distinctive necklace distinguish it; the remaining interchangeable enemies have scene coverage without cards.
Tharandros’s herd is a coordinated migrating group whose collective route changes through the encounter, represented separately from its spokesperson.

The maps, spyglass, die, coin, book, and inscribed staff are retained as distinctive consequential objects; ordinary weapons, armor, provisions, healing consumables, oil, and generic bait animals are excluded.
The goat-knucklebone necklace remains a descriptor of the gnoll leader rather than a separate consequential-item card.
Unspecified clans, generic ancestry groups, the collective creator-god reference, distant unnamed messenger, and unnamed mapmaking uncle are not given separate entity cards.
